page.layout: One printed page (p. 35). Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. Main text in one column running the full width. Margin notes in a narrow column at the right, beside the text. Gathering signature at the foot of the text block.

main_text.p: utantur prædictis nostris legibus, vnusquisque in suo pro curabit iudicio. Proponet autem eam in maxima & regia hac vrbe & eius gloriosissimus Præfectus. Curæ autem erit excellentiss. & laudatissimo nostro magistro, & gloriosiss. atque beatissimis præfectis sacrorum nostrorum Prætoriorum tam his quæ ad solem orientem, quàm his, quæ in Illyride: necnon his etiam, quæ in Libya sunt: per sua edicta his, qui sub ipsis ordinati sunt, ista facere manifesta, ad omnium nostrorum subditorum inexcusabilem notitiam. Data XVII. Kalendas Ianuarias, Domino nostro Iustiniano perpetuo Augusto III. Consule 533.
main_text.head: DE RATIONE ET methodo Iuris docendi ad Antecessores.
main_text.p: IMPERATOR CÆSAR, Flavius, Iustinianus{*}, Alamanicus, Gothicus, Francicus, {b}Germanicus, Anticus, Alanicus, Vandalicus, Africanus, pius, felix, inclytus, victor ac triumphator semper Augustus, Theophilo, Dorotheo, Theodoro, Isidoro, Anatolio, Thalleleo, & Cratino viris illustribus antecessoribus, {c}Item & Salaminio viro disertissimo antecessori Salutem.

OMNEM reipublicæ nostræ sanctionem iam esse purgatam & compositam tam in quatuor libris Institutionum seu elementorum, quam in quinquaginta Digestorum seu Pandectarum, necnon in duodecim Imperialium constitutionum, quis am-plius quam vos cognoscit: Et omnia quidem quæ o-portuerat & ab initio mandare, & post omnium con-summationem, factum libenter admittentes, defini-re, iam per nostras orationes tam Græca lingua qua-

page.notes: Marginal notes (right column), as printed: "* Iustinianus, Apud omnes terræ populos nominatissimum Cæsaris nomen est, & nos præter alias Imperatoriæ maie-statis notas eo gloriamur. Novell. 30." / "b Gallis tamen & Francis non imperabat Iustinianus. arg. l.2.§.2. Co.de off.prop.Afr. Agath.1. c qui sint, vi de §.1.1.co. d ad instar legum. 12. Tabul.Cuiac." The note marks {b} and {c} are placed where the printed letters stand; the mark {d} printed beside the note "ad instar legum" could not be located in the text with certainty. The note text is only partly legible: the citation "Co.de off.prop.Afr." and the "vi de §.1.1.co." fragment may be imperfect. The chapter title is printed without a number, so no caput is given. The text is cut off at the foot of the page at "qua-" and continues on the next page. The initial "O" of OMNEM is an ornamental woodcut letter, read from the trace "MNEM" and the sense of the sentence, so the first letter is uncertain. The word "quis" in "quis amplius" is uncertain.
